integrity: The original full-text preprint was inspected at the exact individual-map equations, slow-nullcline relation, and periodic/chaotic spiking-bursting discussion. A complete same-map chaos paper was inspected through its model equation, fixed-point, Hopf, canard, and chaotic-bursting sections; targeted full-text searches found no covariance, variance, or invariant-measure theorem. A later full open parameter-study article was inspected through its model, Lyapunov, periodicity, and bursting analysis, with no covariance or variance formulation found. The mean law, covariance identity, positive-semidefinite variance bound, equality reflection law, and period-two rigidity were reconstructed independently and replayed with the packaged exact checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem constrains first and second stationary moments rather than the full invariant distribution.
It does not establish existence or uniqueness of chaotic invariant measures for particular parameter values.
The strict equality classification is stated most cleanly for ergodic states with nonzero fast variance; the general equality condition is the almost-sure affine/reflection relation.
The later source used to verify MSC classification concerns coupled Rulkov neurons and is not evidence for the theorem itself.
An equivalent short covariance calculation could remain in unindexed literature.
title: Exact slow–fast covariance law and two-cycle rigidity in the Rulkov neuron map
